steps.intent: France's primary objective is to preserve the legal framework under Chapter VII authorizing maritime interdictions on the high seas off Libya, thereby ensuring the uninterrupted operation of EU Operation IRINI in enforcing the UN arms embargo. The draft maintains a six-month renewal to accommodate the sensitivities and preferences expressed by Libyan authorities, while keeping the Council actively engaged. The main anticipated difficulty lies in persistent skepticism from the Russian Federation, which frequently questions the impartiality and effectiveness of Operation IRINI, as well as the need to secure the support of the A3 members and China without provoking abstentions that could erode Council unity.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

Recalling its resolution 1970 (2011) imposing the arms embargo on Libya and all its subsequent relevant resolutions,

Recalling its resolutions 2292 (2016), 2357 (2017), 2420 (2018), 2473 (2019), 2526 (2020), 2578 (2021), 2635 (2022), 2684 (2023), 2733 (2024), and 2780 (2025) concerning the strict implementation of the arms embargo on the high seas off the coast of Libya,

Reaffirming its resolution 2796 (2025),

Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity of Libya,

Mindful of its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security under the Charter of the United Nations,

Underlining that the implementation of the arms embargo remains essential to support the political process and prevent the proliferation of weapons that fuel conflict and instability in Libya and the wider region,

Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,

1. Decides to extend the authorizations as set out in resolution 2733 (2024) for a further 6 months from the date of this resolution;

2. Requests the Secretary-General to report to the Security Council within five months of the adoption of this resolution on its implementation;

3. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks France and Greece for circulating this draft extending the authorizations under resolution 2733 (2024). As an immediate neighbour of Libya, Algeria consistently underscores the imperative of preserving Libya's sovereignty and ensuring that all multilateral efforts uphold a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned framework. Furthermore, arms embargo enforcement must be balanced and comprehensive across all supply routes to genuinely contribute to regional stability.
messages.China: China supports the strict implementation of the arms embargo on Libya, but the Council must fully listen to the views of the country concerned and address persistent concerns regarding the practical effectiveness and disposal of seized contraband under Operation IRINI. We urge the penholders to reflect these elements in the draft, particularly by ensuring comprehensive reporting and due respect for Libya's sovereignty.
messages.Denmark: Denmark fully supports the draft resolution and thanks the co-penholders, France and Greece, for their continued leadership. Extending the maritime inspection authorizations is critical to curbing the flow of illicit weapons into Libya and ensuring that EU Operation IRINI can effectively carry out its mandate. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text as currently drafted.
messages.Greece: As co-sponsor of this draft resolution alongside France, Greece fully supports the text as circulated. Extending the maritime inspection authorizations under resolution 2292 (2016), as amended by resolution 2733 (2024), remains essential to curbing illicit arms flows to Libya and bolstering regional maritime security, particularly through EU Operation IRINI. We stand ready to work closely with France and all Council members to ensure the swift and unified adoption of this mandate renewal.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft resolution extending the authorizations to enforce the arms embargo off the coast of Libya. We welcome the reaffirmation of Libya's sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity, and we stress that effective implementation of the arms embargo remains critical to supporting a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. We stand ready to work constructively with the co-penholders and other Council members towards a swift adoption.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the six-month extension of the maritime inspection authorizations under resolution 2733 to curb illicit weapons flows and support Libyan stability. In line with our longstanding position on national sovereignty and ownership, we encourage the penholders to incorporate language emphasizing coordination with Libyan authorities and the importance of national capacity-building. We stand ready to work constructively with France and Greece to facilitate the timely adoption of this resolution.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the draft resolution extending the authorizations under resolution 2733 (2024) for another six months. The strict enforcement of the arms embargo on the high seas off the coast of Libya remains critical to curbing illicit weapons flows, supporting national stability, and advancing the UN-led political process. We commend France and Greece for their leadership and stand ready to vote in favour of the text as presented.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea expresses its full support for the draft resolution renewing the maritime interdiction authorizations under resolution 2733 (2024) and commends France and Greece for their constructive leadership as co-penholders. Strict implementation of the arms embargo on the high seas remains indispensable to preventing illicit arms flows, countering regional destabilization, and supporting a viable political process in Libya. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text as currently drafted.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation reiterates its longstanding assessment that the maritime inspection regime established under resolution 2292 (2016) and implemented by EU Operation IRINI has produced no convincing results in halting the flow of weapons into Libya. The mechanism continues to operate selectively while turning a blind eye to arms deliveries entering through land and air corridors. Given the persistent lack of tangible efficacy and transparency, Russia cannot endorse this extension and intends to abstain.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of the high-seas inspection mandate to prevent the illicit flow of weapons into Libya and foster an environment conducive to an inclusive political process. In line with the long-standing position of the A3+, we believe the text should adequately reflect and reinforce the oversight role of the 1970 Sanctions Committee, particularly concerning the transparent handling and disposal of seized items. We look forward to working constructively with the penholders to finalize a balanced resolution.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the draft resolution renewing the authorizations to inspect vessels on the high seas off the coast of Libya suspected of violating the arms embargo. Strict enforcement of the embargo remains critical to preventing the flow of illicit weapons, avoiding escalation, and safeguarding the political process. We thank France and Greece for their leadership on this file and reiterate our strong support for the vital work carried out by EU Operation IRINI.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of the inspection authorizations on the high seas to effectively curb illicit arms flows, but we emphasize that these operations must be conducted with full respect for Libya's sovereignty and territorial integrity. In line with the position of the A3+, we urge the inclusion of language fostering closer coordination with the Libyan authorities and enhancing transparency, particularly regarding the handling and disposal of seized items through the Sanctions Committee. We look forward to engaging constructively with the penholders on this text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports this draft resolution and thanks France and Greece for their leadership. Maintaining the maritime inspection authorizations under resolution 2292 (2016) is essential to countering the illicit flow of weapons and supporting Libya's stability and political process. We endorse the text as currently drafted and stand ready to vote in favour of its adoption.
messages.United States of America: The United States fully supports the draft resolution extending the high seas arms embargo inspection authorizations off the coast of Libya for an additional six months. Enforcing the arms embargo remains critical to preventing illicit weapons proliferation and supporting Libya's stability and political transition. We thank the penholders for circulating a focused, streamlined text and reaffirm our appreciation for the vital maritime interdiction efforts carried out by Operation IRINI.

steps.summary: As co-penholder, France incorporated constructive amendments from Algeria, the A3+ (Sierra Leone, Somalia), Pakistan, and China regarding coordination with Libyan authorities, the role of the 1970 Sanctions Committee, and reporting on the disposal of seized items. These additions preserve the operational integrity of the maritime inspection mandate and EU Operation IRINI while broadening Council consensus, leaving Russia as the likely sole abstention.

The Security Council,

Recalling its resolution 1970 (2011) imposing the arms embargo on Libya and all its subsequent relevant resolutions,

Recalling its resolutions 2292 (2016), 2357 (2017), 2420 (2018), 2473 (2019), 2526 (2020), 2578 (2021), 2635 (2022), 2684 (2023), 2733 (2024), and 2780 (2025) concerning the strict implementation of the arms embargo on the high seas off the coast of Libya,

Reaffirming its resolution 2796 (2025),

Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity of Libya, and emphasizing the importance of a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process,

Emphasizing the importance of close consultation and coordination with the Libyan authorities in the implementation of the arms embargo, and stressing the need to take into full account their views and concerns,

Mindful of its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security under the Charter of the United Nations,

Underlining that the strict and comprehensive implementation of the arms embargo on all routes remains essential to support the political process and prevent the proliferation of weapons that fuel conflict and instability in Libya and the wider region,

messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks the co-penholders, France and Greece, for their constructive efforts on Revision 1. messages.Somalia: Somalia commends the penholders for positively accommodating our proposals in OP2 and throughout the revised text, particularly regarding enhanced coordination with Libyan authorities, transparency, and the role of the 1970 Sanctions Committee. messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports the draft resolution as presented by the penholders. Extending the maritime inspection authorizations is vital for enforcing the arms embargo, preventing illicit weapons flows, and supporting broader security and political stability in Libya. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text without further changes.
messages.United States of America: The United States fully supports the draft resolution renewing the high seas arms embargo inspection mandate for a further six months. Maintaining this authorization is critical to disrupting illicit arms flows, supporting stability in Libya, and reinforcing the work of the Panel of Experts and Operation IRINI. We appreciate the penholders' efforts to preserve this vital security mechanism and are ready to vote in favor of the text as drafted.

before.France:
(spoke in French): The draft resolution submitted today by France and Greece aims to renew for a period of six months the authorizations granted to Member States and regional organizations to inspect vessels on the high seas off the coast of Libya suspected of violating the arms embargo.

As the security situation in Libya remains fragile and volatile, the illicit flow of weapons continues to threaten the stability of the country and the wider Mediterranean region. Strict enforcement of the arms embargo across all routes is vital to support the United Nations-led political process and create conditions conducive to peace and national reconciliation.

In drafting this resolution, France and Greece conducted inclusive consultations with all Council members and engaged closely with the Libyan authorities, taking their views into full account. The text before us reaffirms our collective commitment to Libya’s sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity, while enhancing transparency, coordination, and cooperation with Libyan institutions.

The inspection mechanism, operationalized notably by the European Union’s Operation IRINI, is an essential, impartial, and balanced tool in curbing arms trafficking. We urge all members of the Security Council to vote in favour of this draft resolution.

after.Algeria:
I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the members of the A3+, namely Guyana, Sierra Leone, Somalia, and my own country, Algeria.

At the outset, the A3+ wishes to express its appreciation to the co-penholders, France and Greece, for their efforts and constructive engagement throughout the negotiation process on the resolution that has just been adopted.

The A3+ voted in favour of this resolution to reaffirm our steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity of Libya. We firmly believe that curbing the illicit flow of weapons into Libya is essential to maintaining calm, supporting the ceasefire agreement, and creating an environment conducive to the political process.

In casting our positive vote, the A3+ wishes to highlight several key considerations:

First, the arms embargo on Libya must be applied strictly, impartially, and comprehensively across all domains. While maritime inspections off the coast of Libya serve a purpose, we reiterate that illicit weapons also enter Libya via land and air borders. Council measures cannot be truly effective if they remain partial or selective. Equal vigilance and robust implementation must be applied to all supply routes.

Second, the A3+ underscores the indispensable need for close coordination, consultation, and transparency with the Libyan authorities in the implementation of these authorizations. National ownership must be preserved and respected. Regional organizations and Member States operating under this mandate must act with full transparency, keeping both the Libyan authorities and the 1970 Sanctions Committee duly informed regarding inspections, seizures, and the proper disposal of confiscated materiel. In this regard, we welcome the language included in the text emphasizing dialogue and capacity-building for relevant Libyan institutions.

Finally, the A3+ reaffirms that the arms embargo and security measures are not ends in themselves; they must serve the overarching goal of achieving sustainable peace and stability. The only viable path forward is an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL), leading to free, fair, and transparent presidential and parliamentary elections. We once again urge all external actors to end foreign interference, withdraw all foreign fighters and mercenaries without delay, and respect the will of the Libyan people to determine their own future.

I thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution just adopted. 

The arms embargo on Libya is an important tool for maintaining peace and stability in the country and the wider region. China has consistently called on all parties to strictly and comprehensively implement relevant Security Council resolutions to curb the illicit flow and proliferation of weapons.

In previous discussions, China and several other Council members raised legitimate concerns regarding the practical implementation of maritime inspections under resolution 2292 (2016), in particular the need to respect Libya’s sovereignty, ensure full transparency in the disposal of seized items, and heed the views and concerns of the Libyan authorities. We appreciate that the penholders, France and Greece, listened to the voices of Council members and relevant parties during the consultations and incorporated provisions in the current text that emphasize close consultation and coordination with Libyan authorities, call for transparency regarding the inspection, seizure, and disposal of prohibited material, and request the Secretary-General to report comprehensively on these matters. These positive adjustments reflect our longstanding positions, which enabled China to support the resolution today.

At the same time, China wishes to reiterate that the implementation of the arms embargo must be strict, impartial, and comprehensive across all channels—by sea, land, and air—without selective application or double standards. Regional organizations and Member States carrying out operations authorized by Council resolutions must act strictly within the limits of their mandates, continuously improve operational transparency, strengthen cooperation with Libyan authorities, and avoid any infringement upon the legitimate rights and interests of flag States or the sovereignty of Libya. 

Achieving lasting peace and stability in Libya ultimately depends on advancing a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. The international community must genuinely respect the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Libya, support national reconciliation, and facilitate the early holding of national elections. China stands ready to work with all parties to play a constructive role in restoring peace, stability, and development in Libya.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Denmark:
Denmark welcomes the adoption of the resolution and thanks the co-penholders, France and Greece, for their dedicated and transparent efforts throughout the negotiations to secure the renewal of these vital authorizations.

The illicit flow of weapons and ammunition continues to fuel instability in Libya and pose a serious threat to the wider region. In this fragile context, the robust and impartial implementation of the arms embargo remains essential to de-escalate tensions and create conditions conducive to a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process under United Nations auspices.

As the only operational regional mechanism implementing the maritime inspection authorizations, European Union Naval Force Mediterranean Operation IRINI plays an indispensable role. Through its maritime, aerial, and satellite assets, Operation IRINI contributes directly to deterring illicit trafficking, ensuring accountability, and upholding the decisions of this Council. We also welcome the text's emphasis on close dialogue, cooperation, and transparency with the Libyan authorities, which is vital for building national ownership and long-term stability.

We call on all Member States to fully cooperate with Operation IRINI and strictly comply with their obligations under the arms embargo. Denmark remains steadfast in its support for Libya's sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity, and for the Libyan people's aspirations for lasting peace and unity.
after.Greece:
Greece welcomes the adoption of today’s resolution, which extends for a further six months the vital authorizations to inspect vessels on the high seas off the coast of Libya suspected of violating the arms embargo. 

As co-penholder alongside France, we would like to thank all Council members for their constructive engagement throughout the negotiation process and for their broad support. We also emphasize the importance of our ongoing dialogue and consultations with the Libyan authorities, whose ownership, views, and institutional capacity-building remain essential to achieving sustainable peace and stability.

The legal framework established under resolution 2292 (2016) and subsequent resolutions, including resolution 2733 (2024), remains an indispensable tool for the international community. The illicit flow of arms and related materiel into Libya continues to threaten the country’s fragile security environment, exacerbate political fragmentation, and undermine the prospects for a lasting political settlement. For peace to take root, the arms embargo must be strictly, comprehensively, and effectively enforced across all routes—by sea, land, and air.

In this context, we commend the European Union Naval Force Mediterranean Operation IRINI for its continued, impartial, and effective contribution to the implementation of the arms embargo on the high seas, operating in full compliance with international law and the relevant Security Council mandates. Operation IRINI provides a vital deterrent against illicit arms smuggling and contributes directly to maritime security in the Mediterranean basin.

As an immediate maritime neighbor, Greece remains resolutely committed to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity of Libya. We firmly believe that the only path forward lies in a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations, leading to free, fair, and inclusive national elections. We call on all Libyan parties and international stakeholders to refrain from actions that could undermine stability or violate Council resolutions. 

Greece will continue to work closely with our partners in the Council, regional actors, and the Libyan authorities to support the full implementation of the arms embargo and foster lasting peace and security in Libya and the wider Mediterranean region.
after.Pakistan:
Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted.

Pakistan enjoys close and fraternal ties with Libya and remains steadfastly committed to its sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity. We firmly believe that sustainable peace and stability can only be achieved through an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, supported by the United Nations.

My delegation voted in favour of extending the authorizations under resolution 2733 (2024) to support the comprehensive and effective implementation of the arms embargo and prevent the illicit flow of weapons, which continues to jeopardize peace and security in Libya and the wider region. 

We appreciate the efforts of the co-penholders, France and Greece, to reflect important elements in the text, particularly regarding enhanced coordination and dialogue with the Libyan authorities, the necessity of capacity-building for relevant national institutions, and the emphasis on transparency. 

Moving forward, it remains essential that the arms embargo is implemented in an impartial, objective, and transparent manner, with full respect for Libya’s sovereignty. The 1970 Sanctions Committee must continue to play its central role, including with regard to information-sharing and the proper disposal and destruction of seized items. Furthermore, international efforts must genuinely support national ownership and empower Libyan institutions to eventually assume full responsibility for securing their maritime and territorial borders.

In conclusion, Pakistan reiterates its unwavering support for the brotherly people of Libya in their aspirations for peace, reconciliation, stability, and prosperity.
after.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation abstained in the voting on the draft resolution prepared by France and Greece on extending the authorizations to inspect vessels on the high seas off the coast of Libya.

Russia consistently advocates for strict and unconditional compliance with the arms embargo imposed by Security Council resolution 1970 (2011). We are convinced that stopping the illegal flow of weapons into Libya is one of the most important prerequisites for stabilizing the situation in the country and advancing a comprehensive, Libyan-led political process.

At the same time, we have repeatedly expressed serious reservations regarding the mechanism established under resolution 2292 (2016). When that mechanism was originally authorized, there were hopes that it would serve as an effective instrument in curtailing the influx of weapons. However, years of practical implementation by the European Union’s Operation IRINI have shown that these hopes were largely misplaced. Operation IRINI has demonstrated minimal effectiveness, with results that can hardly justify its maintenance in its current form.

Furthermore, Operation IRINI focuses almost exclusively on the maritime domain, turning a blind eye to the reality on the ground, where the overwhelming majority of illegal weapon transfers occur through land and air corridors. This selective and one-sided approach does not solve the problem of weapon proliferation in Libya; rather, it creates the illusion of activity while serving narrow regional interests. We also note persistent questions regarding the transparency of the operation's activities and the procedures for the storage, disposal, and destruction of seized cargo, as well as the insufficient level of genuine coordination with the Libyan authorities, whose views and sovereign concerns must be respected in full.

Given that these systemic shortcomings have not been addressed, the Russian Federation could not support the resolution and abstained.
after.Sierra Leone:
Sierra Leone voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, renewing for a period of six months the authorizations granted to Member States and regional organizations to inspect vessels on the high seas off the coast of Libya suspected of violating the arms embargo.

Our positive vote reflects our steadfast commitment to peace, stability, and national reconciliation in Libya. Strict and transparent enforcement of the arms embargo remains essential to stemming the illicit flow of weapons and military equipment that continue to fuel divisions and undermine efforts toward lasting peace. 

We commend the co-penholders, France and Greece, for their constructive and inclusive engagement throughout the negotiation process. In particular, we welcome the clear incorporation of provisions reaffirming the primary role of the Committee established pursuant to resolution 1970 (2011), enhancing transparency, and ensuring that the Committee is kept fully informed regarding the inspection, seizure, and disposal of prohibited items. Furthermore, we attach great importance to the strengthened call for close consultation, cooperation, and coordination with the Libyan authorities, which is vital for fostering national ownership and building institutional capacity.

Sierra Leone reiterates that the arms embargo must be implemented comprehensively across all routes—by sea, air, and land. We reaffirm our unwavering support for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity of Libya, and we continue to call upon all international partners to support a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations.
after.Slovenia:
Slovenia welcomes the adoption of the resolution renewing the authorizations for inspections on the high seas off the coast of Libya of vessels suspected of violating the United Nations arms embargo. We voted in favour of the resolution and thank the co-penholders, France and Greece, for their dedicated work and inclusive approach throughout the negotiations.

The security situation in Libya remains fragile and volatile. The continued proliferation and illicit influx of arms and ammunition fuel instability, empower armed groups, and undermine efforts to achieve lasting peace and security. Strict implementation of the United Nations arms embargo on all routes — maritime, land, and air — is essential to prevent further escalation and to support a conducive environment for a viable political process.

In this context, the maritime inspection authorizations remain a vital and practical tool for the international community. We reiterate our strong support for the European Union Naval Force Mediterranean Operation IRINI, which continues to carry out this mandate with professionalism, transparency, and impartiality, in accordance with international law and the relevant Security Council resolutions.

We also welcome the resolution's emphasis on enhanced cooperation, dialogue, and transparency with the Libyan authorities, as well as the importance of capacity-building to support Libyan national ownership. 

Finally, Slovenia reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity of Libya. We urge all Libyan and international stakeholders to engage constructively in a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations, which remains the only viable path to lasting stability and democratic elections.
after.Somalia:
I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the three African members of the Security Council — Algeria, Sierra Leone, and Somalia — as well as Guyana (the A3+).

The A3+ voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends for a further six months the authorizations regarding the inspection of vessels on the high seas off the coast of Libya, in implementation of the arms embargo.

We welcome the constructive approach taken during the negotiations, and we express our appreciation to the co-penholders, France and Greece, for incorporating critical elements that reflect the priorities and shared concerns of our group and of the Libyan people. In particular, we welcome the emphasis placed on full respect for Libya’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity, as well as the call for enhanced dialogue, close consultation, and coordination with the Libyan authorities. 

The A3+ reiterates that the arms embargo must be implemented strictly, comprehensively, and impartially across all domains—maritime, land, and air. Selective enforcement cannot stem the illicit flow of weapons and ammunition that continues to destabilize the country and fuel division. We also reiterate the importance of transparency and accountability in maritime interdictions, including proper reporting to the 1970 Sanctions Committee regarding the seizure, handling, and disposal of intercepted materials.

Ultimately, military measures and maritime inspections cannot substitute for a lasting political solution. We reaffirm our steadfast support for a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations, aimed at overcoming institutional divisions, unifying national institutions, and creating the necessary conditions for holding free, fair, and inclusive national elections. The international community, including regional organizations, must continue to align its efforts behind the aspirations of the Libyan people for peace, security, and stability.

I thank you.
after.United States of America:
The United States voted in favor of today’s resolution to extend for an additional six months the authorizations to inspect vessels on the high seas off the coast of Libya suspected of violating the United Nations arms embargo.

The arms embargo remains a vital tool to curb the illicit flow of weapons and military equipment that fuel instability and conflict in Libya and the wider region. Full and effective implementation of the embargo is essential to support the United Nations-facilitated political process and create the conditions necessary for a unified, sovereign, and stable Libya.

We commend the co-penholders, France and Greece, for their leadership and constructive engagement in shepherding this renewal through the Council. We also express our sincere appreciation to the European Union and the personnel of Operation IRINI for their continued dedication and resources deployed to monitor, deter, and disrupt illicit maritime trafficking off Libya's coast. Operation IRINI provides critical support to the enforcement of Council resolutions and serves an invaluable role in sharing information with the 1970 Sanctions Committee and its Panel of Experts.

The United States calls on all Member States to strictly comply with their obligations under the UN arms embargo and to cease any actions that undermine Libya’s sovereignty or prolong its division. We will continue to work closely with our partners and with the Libyan authorities to help Libya achieve lasting peace, unify its institutions, and secure its own borders.
